title: KV dynamic skew simulator: tokens/sec & p95 regression harness
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a reproducible load-testing harness that synthesizes dynamically skewed access patterns (changing hot keys over time) and variable token payloads to evaluate prefix/KV cache behavior across tokens/sec and p95 latency. The harness will produce baseline profiles, run nightly regression checks, and gate PRs when statistically significant regressions in p95 or tokens/sec are detected.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay 6 canonical workload patterns (steady, ramp, microburst, gradual drift, hotspot rotation, heavy prefix-collisions) against a running prefix cache instance with configurable memory limits.
Exported metrics include tokens_per_sec, requests_per_sec, p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), cache_hit_rate, eviction_rate, memory_used_mb, kv_get_ops and kv_set_ops to Prometheus endpoint.

Nightly regression job compares latest run to baseline using EWMA and two-sample bootstrap on p95 and tokens/sec and opens an automated issue if regression exceeds configurable thresholds (default: p95 +15% or tokens/sec -10%).
CI job runs a fast smoke profile for PR gating (5 min, synthetic hotkey rotation) and fails PRs that show >30% p95 regression on canary models.
Runbook created with clear remediation steps and example parameter knobs (batching, prefetch window, shard count) to test when regressions fire.
test_scenarios: steady_low_concurrency: 50 QPS, uniform prefix distribution, mean token length 60
ramp_up: 10 -> 2000 QPS over 10 minutes with fixed hotkey set (10% traffic), measure p95 slope
microburst: short 30s bursts to 4000 QPS every 5 minutes to assess tail latency under eviction pressure
hotspot_rotation: rotate top-1% hot prefixes every 15 minutes to simulate workload drift and prefix cache warm/cold behavior
prefix_collision_stress: deliberately collide prefixes by truncating hashing to test eviction churn and interference
memory_constrained: limit cache memory to 25% of model KV and observe hit-rate vs p95 tradeoffs
data_generation: Generator produces tokenized requests sampled from a skewed Zipf distribution parameterizable by skew alpha
Payload size distribution supports short (20 tokens), medium (60 tokens), long (256 tokens) with adjustable ratios
Prefix patterns can be supplied from real production fingerprint traces (anonymized) or synthesized via a rotating hotkey list
Support seeded RNG for deterministic replay and ability to snapshot seed + config as a test artifact
instrumentation_and_export: Metrics are emitted via a lightweight client to Prometheus with labels: scenario, run_id, seed, memory_limit_mb, batch_config
p95 is calculated in-process and cross-validated by Prometheus histogram buckets to avoid aggregation errors
Harness pushes structured run metadata to a central S3 bucket for baseline comparison and forensic analysis
Tracing hooks added to record cold vs warm cache path and KV backend latency distributions
regression_detection_method: Primary: EWMA on p95 with configurable smoothing alpha and dynamic control limits derived from 30-run baseline
Secondary: non-parametric bootstrap two-sample test comparing latest run p95 distribution to baseline; reject when p < 0.01
Alerting: create Linear ticket with attached run artifact and Grafana snapshot when either detector trips
Adaptive thresholds: automatically loosen for noisy scenarios (microburst) and tighten for stable steady-state tests
ci_integration: Lightweight smoke run executes in CI on a test harness image (5 minutes, 100 QPS, hotkey rotation) and posts annotated results on the PR
Fail gating rules configured: p95 regression > 30% OR tokens_per_sec drop > 25% compared to ephemeral baseline for the branch
Artifacts (Prometheus scrape, run metadata) uploaded to the PR for reviewer inspection
Nightly pipeline runs full candidate suite and updates baseline snapshots on successful benchmark stability (manual approval required)
rollout_and_mitigation: When regression ticket is opened, automated minimap suggests likely knobs to run next (increase prefetch window, shrink batch size, increase memory cap)
Priority triage run: re-run failing scenario with isolated variables to determine sensitivity and shortest remediation path
If regression correlates to a kernel or runtime change, require a canary rollback and postmortem with latency breakdown
Documented rollback checklist included in runbook: how to pin model variant, how to increase dedicated capacity, how to disable new kernel flag
